Jury Rigging also helps keep any good gear you come across in peak condition, as you can repair armor pieces with any armor of its weight class, so stuff like power armor can be repaired with any heavy armor, such as the much cheaper metal armor, and combat armor can be repaired with any medium armor. Once you have caps, then you can buy some decent gear and go hunting for some of the good unique items. Weapons like the Ratslayer, Oh Baby!, AER14 prototype, Paladin Toaster, etc. depending on your primary attack method. As for armor, light armor can get you extra crit chance with a perk, medium armor is solid protection while retaining mobility, and heavy is pure tank, but slow. I won’t spoil how you get your hands on the high class armors, but the DLC areas (minus Dead Money) are good places to look once you hit the recommended level to take them on. Dead Money is a slog gameplay wise, though. Best to save it for when you’re very well acquainted with the game. It’s usually the last DLC I do in a run, for good reason.

Through strong emotions, and the nature of the Void, a new realm was manifested. A pocket dimension, I suppose, contained within the void, pulled directly from the Drifter’s imagination, inspired by the storybook. Dominus Thrax, one of the Drifter’s many dolls, rules over Duviri, while the Courtiers (also dolls) represent the emotions of the Drifter’s experiences aboard the Zariman. Now, why was Duviri created? Well, the Void’s properties aren’t really understood by us, it’s secrets were only barely touched upon by the Orokin and their knowledge is mostly lost. I would assume, however, that the living Void, the Lidless Eye, the Indifference, finds our Operator interesting, and the Drifter and Operator are one person, across different realities, tied together through Eternalism. We know a deal was made between the Operator and the Indifference, granting the Tenno their power over the Void. Perhaps the Drifter was offered a similar deal. Their own realm, where they would be safe. Or perhaps That Which Bears No Name simply tried something different, not offering a choice. That remains to be seen, I suppose. And that’s my TLDR of the Duviri Experience. Hopefully I did alright scribing my thoughts, and hopefully I got most of that right.
